name: Basilika Wilten
kurzbeschreibung: The Wilten Basilica in Innsbruck is celebrated as one of Austria's finest Rococo churches, adorned with pastel stuccowork and Marian pilgrimage heritage.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Wilten Basilica—officially the Parish and Pilgrimage Church of Our Lady under the Four Columns—is a breathtaking baroque and early classical masterpiece nestled at the southern edge of Innsbruck. Rising adjacent to the venerable Premonstratensian Wilten Abbey, it is widely acclaimed as one of the most harmonious and refined Rococo church edifices in the entire alpine realm. The magnificent sacred landmark emanates a luminous, serene spiritual atmosphere that has inspired worshippers, art historians, and travelers from around the globe for centuries. Honoring its historic and theological significance, Pope Pius XII elevated the sanctuary to the dignity of a papal Basilica minor in 1957. As the ancient mother parish of Innsbruck, this sacred ground boasts continuous Christian worship reaching back to late Roman antiquity.

Route & Requirements

Archaeological investigations demonstrate that a late Roman-Christian church already stood here in the 5th century within the fortified Roman outpost of Veldidena. Beginning in 1140, the Premonstratensian canons of Wilten Abbey assumed pastoral care. Marian pilgrimages are documented since 1259, centered around the revered 14th-century late-Gothic sandstone statue of Our Lady under the Four Columns enthroned beneath an ornate gilded canopy. The present church was constructed between 1751 and 1756 based on designs by Joseph Stapf under the supervision of church architect Franz de Paula Penz. Master craftsmen shaped its interior: plasterers Franz Xaver Feuchtmayer and Anton Gigl created graceful rocailles in delicate pink, white, and gold, while Bavarian court painter Matthäus Günther executed vibrant ceiling frescoes depicting scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary.

Visit & Arrival

The Wilten Basilica is open daily throughout the year from 07:30 to 18:00 (tourist visits are paused during religious services). Admission is free; donations for church preservation are gratefully received. Public transit: from downtown Innsbruck, take tram line 1 directly to the Bergisel stop (3 minutes walk to the church) or the Stubaitalbahn (STB) to Stift Wilten. By car: via autobahn A12 (exit Innsbruck-Mitte/Wilten) or A13 (Innsbruck-Süd); paid parking is available along Bergiselweg and around the abbey precinct.

Tips

A step-free side entrance accessible from the paved church forecourt allows smooth, barrier-free access for wheelchair users and families with strollers. Following your visit, stroll through the tranquil historic Wilten cemetery where notable Tyrolean figures rest. Be sure to explore Wilten Abbey directly across the square and experience the soaring sacred music during Sunday orchestral High Masses.
